title: Isolated single-connection reconnect, ETL and Nirvana

methods.sample: One existing resolved edge alternates between its original target and a distinct valid target. No add, delete or selection operation.
methods.cadence: Ten warm operations precede each 100-operation measured run. Each next input waits at least 100 ms after the previous input plus two requestAnimationFrame callbacks. MiniMap layer count is asserted zero.
methods.clock: performance.now in the page. Input-to-rAF is completion of the first requested callback after the public API mutation; it is not physical input-to-photon or a compositor-present timestamp.
methods.phases: Top-level timers only. Scheduler includes backend work; backend and named nested phases must not be added. GPU time is sampled every sixth operation using EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2; samples are asynchronous.
methods.statistics: Arithmetic median and discrete p95 = sorted[floor(0.95*n)]. Raw timing values are rounded to six decimal places in milliseconds.
methods.quality: Full main WebGL framebuffer readPixels at fixed scene time 2.5; does not include HTML layers or MiniMap. Both overview and scale 0.35 include before, forward and restored states.
methods.ordering: Separate browser launches, reference/candidate/candidate/reference ordering per fixture. Cold mount is excluded from the measured operations.
methods.memory: Typed overlap arrays count unique backing buffers once, including shared box/out subarrays. Path capacities are counters, not a full retained-heap measurement. heapReported is coarse performance.memory and must not be interpreted as a GC-normalized heap result.

fixture.note: The saved Nirvana graph is reused exactly. To repeat on another machine, freeze one generated fixture and use that identical input for both builds; do not compare independent random generations.

limitations: Timing uses a public API mutation rather than a physical pointer gesture.
This is one explicitly recorded edge and target pair in each fixture, including a long cross-graph retarget; it is not a distribution over arbitrary edges.
The main-framebuffer equality checks do not validate HTML compositing.
Per-source buckets and mixed-plan work can still depend on scene size; the optimization does not establish constant-time retargeting.

diagnostic.warning: The reference diagnostic source-snapshot identity fields are stale because the helper mutated snapshots in place. Only immutable sorted-list equality, overlap revisions, changed IDs and fallback fields are used as evidence. Diagnostic timers are not headline timings.

verification.provenance: Final functional check results supplied by the implementation owners, separately from this performance acquisition.
